evidence.text: Amazon's Q3 2026 report (2026-10-29) kept 2026 cash capex at about $220B. Jassy said Amazon expects to spend 'meaningfully more in 2027', the chips business is growing at triple-digit rates, and Trainium revenue commitments are up more than 20x year on year. Amazon holds a purchase-vesting warrant on up to $6.5B of Astera products and is very likely Astera's largest customer (Customer A is 29% of Q2 revenue in the 10-Q). This supports a Q4 guide at or above the ~$656m bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line has not paid recently. In August a guide of $540-560m against $410m consensus (+34%) still fell 11.96% over the window, after a +20%/+12.7% run-in (Trefis). In February the stock fell 21.41%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market read Amazon's print as an AI-ROI worry: ALAB fell 10.9-11.7% on 2026-10-30, about four times the Nasdaq, with no company news (TIKR). If the demand read-through were priced, ALAB would have held up against the semis tape. It went the other way. Whether Astera's Q4 guide carries Trainium3 volume is first visible on the call.
evidence.independence: Amazon's demand statements also appear in the datastudios Q3 write-up (https://www.datastudios.org/post/amazon-q3-2026-results-aws-39-percent-growth-46-billion-220-billion-capex). Astera's own Q2 10-Q shows vested Amazon warrant shares accelerating from 1,165,513 (Dec) to 1,331,902 (Mar) to 1,663,042 (Jun), which tracks Amazon purchases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001736297/000173629726000035/alab-20260630.htm). That is a separate document but the same customer. The transmission from Amazon capex to Astera's Q4 is a proxy.

evidence.text: Celestica, a major hyperscaler AI-rack assembler, reported Q3 2026 revenue of $5.83B on 2026-10-26, above its $5.25-5.55B guide, with CCS up 102%. It guided Q4 to $6.275-6.575B and set a first 2027 outlook of about $40B (+90%), saying customers' 2028 forecasts are meaningfully higher. That is a broad, current AI-hardware demand read for the rack programmes Astera's switches and retimers go into.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history of ALAB reacting to Celestica. ALAB fell about 11% in the week after this print, so the market did not pass it through.
evidence.why_not_priced: ALAB is down 38% in 20 days while a direct supply-chain peer guided 2027 up 90%. Had the read-through been priced, ALAB's drawdown would not sit beside a peer raising its outlook. The market treated ALAB as AI beta, not as a demand read.
evidence.independence: This is a different company and document from the Amazon finding but the same end-demand theme. Celestica does not name Astera, so this is a proxy.

evidence.text: Microsoft now expects calendar-2026 capex of about $170B, down from its earlier outlook (about $190B in earlier guidance), because third-party data-center capacity is delayed. This is a negative datapoint for the AI-hardware supply chain, though Microsoft is not confirmed as a top Astera customer.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to ALAB. It arrived in the same Oct 29-30 window as ALAB's -11% day.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it was part of the Oct 29-30 AI selloff. It is filed so the set nets the Amazon and Celestica positives against the one hyperscaler that cut. It matters only if Astera's Q4 guide shows a non-Amazon customer slowing.
evidence.independence: Same HL/Business Insider article as the Amazon finding (one document, two facts pointing in opposite directions). The earlier ~$190B Microsoft figure is from search snippets (Luminix, https://www.useluminix.com/reports/industry-analysis/hyperscaler-capex-q3-2026/source/4).

evidence.text: The setup is the reverse of August. Then the stock rose about 20% on 2026-07-30 and 12.7% on print day before falling 12%; Trefis wrote that 'the rally came first'. This time it goes in down 38.3% in 20 days and 16.1% in 5, about 50% below its high, with no company-specific news (TIKR 2026-10-20 and 2026-11-03; the semis selloff took Credo -14% and Marvell -11% in one October week). It trades at 46x forward earnings, near the bottom of its range (March low 41x, one-year average 72x).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The three most recent prints (Feb -21.4%, May -0.8%, Aug -12.0%) were all sold. Aug 2025 (+28.7%) came after a weak tape; ALAB moved up on only 2 of its last 7 prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced by construction, since the drawdown is the price. The point is that the 'beats get sold' prior in the baseline was measured after run-ups, and this print comes after a run-down. If the market expected a clean guide, the stock would not have fallen 36% since 2026-10-07 on sector news. The put skew is only moderate (+6.2), and put/call OI of 0.55 does not show heavy protection demand.
evidence.independence: TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/astera-labs-fell-harder-than-the-market-in-the-ai-selloff-heres-what-november-3-must-show) gives the 46x forward multiple and the no-company-news attribution. [sizing note removed].

evidence.text: The Q2 2026 10-Q shows work-in-progress inventory nearly tripled, from $35.8m (Dec 2025) to $98.7m (Jun 2026), with total inventory at $113.8m. Vested Amazon warrant shares rose 1.17M to 1.33M to 1.66M over two quarters. Both corroborate the guided Q3 Scorpio X ramp. The inventory build also explains why Q2 free cash flow, $67.2m, was about half the prior-year level.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 revenue beat the guide midpoint by about 9% and the stock fell 12%. Ramp corroboration of this kind has not been paid.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the result sits inside what the company guided ($540-560m). It is filed because it tells against a Q3 shortfall, and an inventory build of this size would be visible as a write-down risk if the ramp had slipped.
evidence.independence: TIKR 2026-10-20 reports Q2 FCF of $67.2m, about half the prior year (https://www.tikr.com/de/blog/astera-labs-lost-11-in-a-week-stifel-sees-60-upside-from-here). That is the same fact seen through cash flow, so the two are merged into this finding.

evidence.text: Gross margin is stepping down. Non-GAAP GM was guided to about 72% for Q3, against 73.7% in Q2 and 76.3% in Q1, and the CFO has said margins trend 'down towards the 70% range' as hardware modules and Scorpio grow and the Amazon warrant contra-revenue grows ($10.2m in Q2, against $2.1m in 1H25). A Q4 GM guide below 72% is the likely flashpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In August the GM guide fell from about 74% to 72% and the stock fell 12% the next session. Trefis attributes that move to the run-up rather than the margin.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus models about 72.6% GM for 2026 (TIKR), above where the CFO says margins are heading. A high-60s or roughly 70% Q4 GM guide would be under that, and the multiple has nowhere to hide if the narrative becomes 'hardware-ization'.
evidence.independence: The Q2 8-K gives the 72% guide and the 73.7% actual (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001736297/000173629726000033/q226exhibit991.htm). The Q2 10-Q gives the warrant contra-revenue of $10.2m. Three documents, one line.

evidence.text: Astera habitually beats its own guide. Q2 revenue was $392.4m against a $355-365m guide (+9% on the midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS $0.80 against $0.68-0.70 (+16%). Q3 consensus sits at the $551m guide midpoint and $1.19 EPS, so the reported quarter will likely clear it; a repeat of the Q2 pattern implies about $590m. The beat is the expected outcome, not a surprise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three revenue beats were all sold: -21.4%, -0.8% and -12.0% (TIKR headline 'Stock Fell After Its Last 3 Revenue Beats').
evidence.why_not_priced: The published consensus at the midpoint understates the habitual beat. The buy side expects a beat, though, and the reaction history says a beat alone does not move the stock up. The finding is kept small for that reason.
evidence.independence: The Q2 actuals are in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001736297/000173629726000033/q226exhibit991.htm).

evidence.text: BLS CPI for car and truck rental was +9.1% YoY in September 2026 (+0.1% MoM), while Avis guided Q3 RPD to 'roughly flat' YoY on the Q2 call. If even a third of that industry pricing reached Avis's Americas RPD (Q3 2025 $73.19), the Q3 revenue/RPD bar ($3.41-3.46B, which embeds flat RPD and fewer days) would be beaten.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The name sells prints: 1 up of the last 7 (median |move| 6.8%). On Q3 2025, revenue beat estimates with RPD -1% ex-FX and the stock fell 6.06% (baseline; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/avis-budget-stock-declines-11-despite-reporting-q3-earnings-beat). On Q2 2026, record utilization and flat RPD gave -6.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Neither the company guide nor the consensus revenue (down 2-3% YoY) carries any RPD uplift. If the market had priced a pricing beat, the stock would not be -33% since 7/30 with analysts cutting targets into the print, and the skew would not be +8.3 put-rich. The caveat: CPI rental also includes truck rental and did not track Avis's flat Q2 RPD, and Avis is deliberately shifting mix toward longer, lower-RPD rentals, so it is filed as a proxy and sized small.
evidence.independence: Separate sources point to travel-price inflation from the 2026 fuel shock: Delta domestic unit revenue +16% in Q3 (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx?type=bn), and Hertz Q2 2026 RPD +9% YoY (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001657853/000165785326000045/q22026earningsrelease.htm). evidence.text: TSA checkpoint volume for June 21-Sept 7 2026 was 204.15M against 209.91M a year earlier (-2.7%), with August -4.4%, as fuel-driven airfares rose (Delta Q3 adjusted unit revenue +15%, United revenue +17.4% on 1.3% capacity). Fewer air travellers means less airport rental volume, Avis's core channel.
evidence.source_date: 2026-09 (summer 2026 analysis; page fetch returned 403, figures from the search snippet)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume misses have been sold. On Q2 2026, rental days fell 2% with bookings trailing expectations and the stock fell 6.9% (baseline; https://www.autorentalnews.com/news/avis-cuts-fleet-as-summer-demand-trails-expectations).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partly inside the guide: the company already guided the Americas fleet down mid-single digits for Q3 and said summer bookings trailed expectations. What may not be priced is that August, the peak month, fell harder (-4.4%) than the July run-rate the company could see when it spoke on 7/28. If the market had fully priced it, revenue consensus would sit nearer -4% than -2-3%.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Corroborated by Avis's own Q2 call ('inbound travel fell below initial expectations', https://www.autorentalnews.com/news/avis-cuts-fleet-as-summer-demand-trails-expectations). The fare data comes from the airline 8-Ks/RTTNews, a different source.

The bar is not sourced (no EBITDA consensus found), so this is capped small and the wide range carries the uncertainty. Shrunk for the crowded short.

On 2026-11-02 it noticed redemption of all $350M of its 5.750% 2027 senior notes for 2026-12-30, about $20M of annual interest. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The settlement news gave an overnight rise of 5.22% when announced (https://www.itiger.com/news/1104931090). No print reaction history on leverage.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: both 8-Ks are public. What the money buys is debt reduction, not a ramp. What may be unpriced is the call's update of the leverage path and any buyback or further redemption from the remaining ~$300M. If priced fully, the 10/06 pop would not have faded into a -33% drawdown. The gain is a one-off below operating income, so it is [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: The 2026-10-06 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723612/000095014226002687/eh260839574_8k.htm) is the same company source. The Q2 call states the leverage target (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/CAR-2Q26-AI-Summary).

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to fleet ABS issuance.
evidence.why_not_priced: What the money buys: refinancing of the domestic fleet, with no distress signal, so it is near zero. Its only edge is that Q4 vehicle-interest guidance could edge up. If it were a signal, the ABS would have priced wide or been upsized, and it was not reported that way.
evidence.independence: none

That weighs on drive-leisure rental demand and on residuals of the less fuel-efficient fleet, and raises shuttle and operating fuel cost.

evidence.text: The FTC plus eight states (CA, CO, FL, IL, IA, NE, OK, UT) sued Toast on 2026-10-29 in N.D. Cal. under the FTC Act and ROSCA. evidence.why_not_priced: The suit itself is priced (a -1.4% day, then fully recovered). The rebound past the pre-suit price says the market assumes neither.

evidence.text: Management guided Q3 2026 to high-single-digit revenue growth, above its old mid-single-digit guides, and said growth would keep accelerating ('5% to 10% to 15% to 20%'). evidence.text: The CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor (card data from ~120M cards), released 2026-10-08, had furniture and home furnishings down 2.7% y/y in September 2026, the only category that fell, while total retail rose ~4% y/y. In July 2026 the same category was +2.71% y/y. That points to the home category weakening through the quarter. Wayfair's guide assumed flat macro ('bouncing along the bottom') and share gains.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved case in the baseline of a macro category print leading Wayfair's own revenue. Wayfair has grown through flat-to-down category data in 2025-26 on claimed share gains (Q2 2026 US +8.7%).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a proxy, not company data: the category counts store-based furniture retailers (with their own online sales), not nonstore pure plays like Wayfair. The new methodology also breaks comparison with earlier months, so July and September are not on the same basis. It is public, but analysts have not cut Q3 revenue below the guide midpoint, so it has not reached consensus. If it had been priced, consensus would sit at the low end of HSD (~$3.34B) and the 20d run-up would not be +5.4%.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. July's +2.71% comes from a different NRF release: https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/cnbc-nrf-retail-monitor-shows-10th-month-of-sales-growth-in-july. No company or counterparty confirmation.

evidence.text: Amazon's Q3 2026 online stores sales grew only ~2% y/y ($68.47B vs $67.41B), about +6% adjusting for Prime Day moving from July 2025 (Q3) into Q2 2026. That leaves Wayfair facing a July 2025 comp that an analyst on the Q2 call called 'a really tough comp in July', with no Prime Day halo or competing event in July 2026. Management guided HSD knowing the calendar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record for a peer calendar shift.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced and inside the guide: Wayfair knew the July comp when it guided on 2026-08-04. The sign is ambiguous, because less Prime Day competition in July could also help. If the shift were a known Wayfair headwind, consensus would sit below the HSD midpoint.
evidence.independence: Amazon's own release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000038/amzn-20260930xex991.htm ; the tough-July-comp remark is in the Q2 transcript (different document).

Its YoY growth in Q3 still benefits from the distributor acquisition, which closed late in Q3 2025 (Q3 2025 China base $10.1m). The risk is sequential: China below ~$15m.

evidence.why_not_priced: Macro proxy for 11% of revenue. The guide assumed 'consistent trends in APAC', and a slightly worse China market is only a few-point deterioration, which no estimate visibly reflects. Net of the rest: the US (55%) and Canada would have to hold ~11% growth for total revenue to clear the guide, and a $1-2m China shortfall is ~1% of revenue.
